CEG
CEG
Constellation Energy
Added Oct 31
 Net long
Nov 20 expiry
 Power demand from data centers keeps lifting what Constellation's nuclear fleet can earn.
Wrong if: CEG closes below $242.64 (the stop), or the Nov 9 report shows no new data-center contract news and the stock gives back the gap.
What proves it: CEG closes above $271.77 at the Nov 20 expiry.
Why we hold this view: Our view (OPINION): the market still prices Constellation like a regular power company, while data-center buyers are paying up for round-the-clock carbon-free power. The Nov 9 report is part of the idea. We hold through it because new or extended data-center power contracts there are the most likely thing to move the stock toward $290, and the spread caps the loss at $1,176.67 if it disappoints.

GEV
GEV
GE Vernova
Added Nov 5
 Net long
Jan 15, 2027 expiry
 Turbine slots stay scarce and data-center gas pricing keeps rising.
Notes: The 860 call had 21 contracts traded and a $6.00-wide market at entry; the 900 call had more activity (844 contracts). Held to expiry.
Wrong if: GEV finishes at or below $860 at expiry (the whole debit is lost), or slot reservations stop turning into firm orders and turbine pricing rolls over.
What proves it: GEV closes at or above $900 at the Jan 15, 2027 expiry, so the spread earns its $2,580 maximum profit.
Why we hold this view: Our view (OPINION): for the next 12 to 24 months an AI chip is only worth as much as the energized megawatt under it, and the turbine delivery slot is the cleaner uncapped upside versus PJM's capped capacity price. The debit spread caps the loss at $1,420.
